fuente: Icfes — Cuadernillo de preguntas Saber Pro, Módulo de Inglés (2018)

contextos.texto:
**Lea las descripciones de la columna de la izquierda (1 - 5). ¿Cuál palabra de la columna de la derecha (A - H) concuerda con cada descripción? Una opción (A - H) se usa para el ejemplo. Sobran dos palabras más.**

**Feelings**

Ejemplo:

0. Some people feel this way when they see spiders because they don't like them.

Respuesta: 0. A

- **A.** afraid
- **B.** angry
- **C.** cold
- **D.** happy
- **E.** hungry
- **F.** sad
- **G.** thirsty
- **H.** tired

**Complete las cinco conversaciones.**

Ejemplo:

— What time does the train arrive at the station?

- A. In two hours.
- B. The second one.
- C. Right there.

Respuesta: 0. A

**Lea el texto de la parte inferior y seleccione la palabra correcta para cada espacio.**

**GREEK AND ROMAN CULTURES**

The Greek culture, together with the Roman one, (0) ____ fascinated humans for centuries. Sadly, many people today (11) ____ know the differences between Greeks and Romans.

Some people think Romans are an extension of Greeks; others assume that the two are similar. In fact, the two are very different (12) ____ one another, and show opposite life values.

(13) ____ Greeks and Romans were great architects. Greeks used to (14) ____ more about shape than function. They (15) ____ the most important thing was making beautiful buildings. (16) ____, Romans were perfect engineers. For (17) ____, street planning and use had the greatest importance.

Greeks admired poets and philosophers, (18) ____ Romans admired their soldiers who were extremely brave and successful.

Ejemplo: 0. A. have — B. having — C. had. Respuesta: 0. A

contextos.titulo: Parte 5 — A Social Experiment in Oneida, New York
contextos.texto:
**Lea el artículo y luego responda las preguntas.**

**A SOCIAL EXPERIMENT IN ONEIDA, NEW YORK**

In the nineteenth century there was a village called Oneida in New York State where a "family" of 300 members lived together in a large beautiful house where they shared everything.

A man named John Humphrey Noyes, and a small group of people moved there in 1848. They wanted a place where they could live according to their particular beliefs in their efforts to create a more equal society.

Today, this place is touristic and, like me, many visitors come because they had relatives among those 19th century dreamers. Others just want to see for themselves the building where this successful social group in American history lived. “I don’t know of anywhere else where you can live in a historical place,” said the director of the Oneida site. “It’s very unusual.”

The present owners share the building with guests who stay in large comfortably furnished bedrooms with private baths. There are eight guest rooms in the hotel area, and each guest pays $100 for a big bedroom, a simple breakfast and a private tour of the 10,300-square-meter building, which also contains 35 apartments.

The library and the building’s grounds are also open to guests, as well as several of the public rooms. The 170-year-old library, unchanged from the original construction, holds a rich collection of 19th century books and magazines, which learners used to study Latin, Greek, algebra and astronomy.

This place is open for everybody and it’s worth a visit.

Ejemplo: 0. Something unusual about the Oneida village place is that — A. everybody slept under the same roof. B. people were very independent. C. everyone had their own room. Respuesta: 0. A

preguntas.enunciado: People often cry when they feel like this.
preguntas.explicacion: **sad** significa «triste»; la gente suele llorar cuando está triste.

preguntas.enunciado: If we feel like this, we want to eat something.
preguntas.explicacion: **hungry** significa «con hambre»; cuando tenemos hambre queremos comer algo.

preguntas.enunciado: When we hate something, we sometimes feel like this.
preguntas.explicacion: **angry** significa «enojado»; odiar algo suele producir enojo.

preguntas.enunciado: Some people usually feel like this when it's hot, and need to drink something.
preguntas.explicacion: **thirsty** significa «sediento»; con calor se siente sed y se necesita beber.

preguntas.enunciado: A person feels like this when they need to sleep after a long day.
preguntas.explicacion: **tired** significa «cansado»; tras un día largo uno está cansado y necesita dormir.

preguntas.enunciado: Do you prefer cats or dogs?
preguntas.explicacion: Ante una pregunta de preferencia entre dos opciones, *Both are nice* («ambos son lindos») es una respuesta lógica; las otras no responden a la elección.

preguntas.enunciado: I forgot to turn the lights off.
preguntas.explicacion: Ante la afirmación de haber olvidado apagar las luces, lo natural es pedir confirmación: *Are you sure?* («¿Estás seguro?»).

preguntas.enunciado: I am afraid my sister is sick.
preguntas.explicacion: Ante una mala noticia (la hermana está enferma) se expresa empatía con *Oh, I’m sorry* («lo siento»).

preguntas.enunciado: Let’s go to the park next weekend.
preguntas.explicacion: *Let’s…* es una propuesta; la respuesta adecuada es aceptarla: *Great idea* («¡buena idea!»).

preguntas.enunciado: Can I talk to you for a minute?
preguntas.explicacion: Es una petición de permiso; *Of course* («claro») la concede de forma natural.

preguntas.enunciado: Hueco (11): Sadly, many people today (11) ____ know the differences between Greeks and Romans.
preguntas.explicacion: El sujeto *many people* es plural y la frase está en presente (*today*), por lo que se usa **don’t**.

preguntas.enunciado: Hueco (12): In fact, the two are very different (12) ____ one another, and show opposite life values.
preguntas.explicacion: La colocación correcta es **different from** («diferente de»).

preguntas.enunciado: Hueco (13): (13) ____ Greeks and Romans were great architects.
preguntas.explicacion: **Both … and …** («tanto … como …», «ambos») acompaña a dos sujetos unidos por *and* con verbo plural *were*.

preguntas.enunciado: Hueco (14): Greeks used to (14) ____ more about shape than function.
preguntas.explicacion: Después de **used to** va el verbo en forma base: *used to worry* («solían preocuparse»).

preguntas.enunciado: Hueco (15): They (15) ____ the most important thing was making beautiful buildings.
preguntas.explicacion: El texto habla del pasado (*used to*, *was*), así que se requiere el pasado **believed**.

preguntas.enunciado: Hueco (16): (16) ____, Romans were perfect engineers.
preguntas.explicacion: Se contrasta a los griegos (forma) con los romanos (ingeniería); el conector de contraste es **However** («sin embargo»).

preguntas.enunciado: Hueco (17): For (17) ____, street planning and use had the greatest importance.
preguntas.explicacion: El pronombre se refiere a *Romans* (plural) después de preposición: **them**.

preguntas.enunciado: Hueco (18): Greeks admired poets and philosophers, (18) ____ Romans admired their soldiers who were extremely brave and successful.
preguntas.explicacion: Las dos ideas se oponen (poetas y filósofos frente a soldados), por eso se usa el conector de contraste **but**.

preguntas.enunciado: John Humphrey Noyes travelled to New York State

opciones.B: to change his way of life.
opciones.C: to know more about his country.

preguntas.explicacion: El texto dice que querían un lugar para vivir *according to their particular beliefs* y crear una sociedad más igualitaria, es decir, cambiar su forma de vida.

preguntas.enunciado: Nowadays Oneida is
preguntas.explicacion: Hoy los dueños comparten el edificio con huéspedes: *There are eight guest rooms in the hotel area* y cada uno paga $100 por habitación y desayuno.

preguntas.enunciado: The writer visited the place because he

opciones.B: had family who had lived there.

preguntas.explicacion: El autor dice *like me, many visitors come because they had relatives among those 19th century dreamers*: tenía familiares que vivieron allí.

preguntas.enunciado: If you want to see the building,

opciones.A: you need to pay to have a guided visit.
opciones.B: you can join a small group of people.
opciones.C: you will have your own guide included.

preguntas.explicacion: El pago de $100 incluye *a private tour of the 10,300-square-meter building*, es decir, un recorrido guiado privado incluido.

preguntas.enunciado: All visitors to the Oneida historical site

opciones.A: have access to most parts of the house.
opciones.B: have to go to the 19th century library.
opciones.C: are not allowed to see certain places.

preguntas.explicacion: La biblioteca, los terrenos y varias salas públicas están abiertos a los huéspedes, y *This place is open for everybody*: pueden acceder a la mayor parte de la casa.

preguntas.enunciado: The old library
preguntas.explicacion: El texto la describe como *unchanged from the original construction*: ha permanecido igual.

preguntas.enunciado: People at Oneida studied
preguntas.explicacion: Los estudiantes usaban los libros para estudiar *Latin, Greek, algebra and astronomy*; latín y griego son idiomas.
